display.purpose: Landing hero title and the Reverend Insanity wordmark across the site in consistent upright Times New Roman.

headline.purpose: Chapter titles in /read and section headlines across Landing and Account.

title.purpose: Dialog/drawer headers and individual book volume cards.

body.purpose: Sustained multi-chapter novel reading and editorial synopsis blocks with kern, liga, and oldstyle figures.

ui-body.purpose: Interactive chrome, buttons, comments, modals, and form fields (16px minimum on mobile inputs).

label.purpose: Uppercase small-caps eyebrows, volume badges, and metadata captions.

mono-telemetry.purpose: Tabular chapter counters, reaction tallies, and word count indicators that must never jitter.

reader-literary.purpose: Optional Literata digital-edition serif preset in reader font selector.

reader-dyslexic.purpose: Optional OpenDyslexic reader typeface preset improving character distinction.

shadows.name: pop

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Modal sheets (Settings, Chapters TOC, Info) and slide-over Comments drawer.

narrative.overview:
Reverend Reader treats an unforgiving 2,334-chapter dark fantasy novel with the stillness and discipline of a stitched manuscript edition. Rather than wrapping reading in terminal neon gradients, orbital hero chrome, or sticky engagement badges, the interface steps backward until only warm paper, crisp carbon ink, and a sparse cinnabar chop remain. Reading prose is the primary surface; every navigation rail, bookmark control, and community drawer is designed to recede cleanly when prose begins.

Mobile phones are the first-priority environment. On viewports below `640px`, controls consolidate into a unified docked bottom thumb bar balanced against a compact header so thumbs never hunt upward across the glass and prose preserves generous horizontal breathing room. On tablet and desktop viewports, navigation expands into a symmetric header paired with a whisper-quiet right interaction rail, never breaking the centered reading measure.
keyCharacteristics: Tactile manuscript warmth in daylight (`#faf8f3` paper and `#af1d27` vermilion chop) paired with restrained OLED charcoal (`#0d0f0e`) and muted antique gold (`#d0be94`) at night.
Literary serif hierarchy led by Bookerly and EB Garamond for titles and long-form prose, disciplined by DM Sans chrome and tabular JetBrains Mono numerals.
Crisp 1px hairline containment and tonal surface steps (`paper` -> `surface` -> `sunken`) instead of heavy elevation drop shadows.

Mobile-first thumb ergonomics (`44px–48px` primary targets, non-zooming `16px` mobile inputs, `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` clearance) with instant zero-gate access to both English and Chinese editions.

rules.name: The One-Chop Rule
rules.body: Reserve the vermilion (or antique gold in dark mode) fill exclusively for the primary reading action, active selection indicator, and inline `蛊` seal mark; secondary actions stay neutral ink over hairline borders so accent never exceeds roughly 10% of the viewport.

rules.name: The AA Paper Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every scoped dark or tinted reader surface inside `[data-reader-surface]` rebinds `--paper`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--muted`, `--line`, and `--accent` locally in CSS so headings, links, and footer buttons stay readable (`>= 4.5:1`) regardless of global light or dark theme; the `#e4e8f0` sentinel acts solely as Auto Ink and never forces pale gray ink onto daylight or translucent surfaces.

rules.name: The Tabular Counter Rule
rules.body: Apply `tabular-nums lining-nums` (`tnum`) to every chapter number, reaction count, percentage readout, and word count so live progress updates and adjacent columns never shift laterally.

rules.name: The Anti-Zoom Input Rule
rules.body: Render interactive `<input>`, `<textarea>`, and `<select>` elements at `16px` (`text-base`) on viewports below `640px`, stepping down to `14px` (`sm:text-sm`) only on desktop so mobile Safari and Chrome never pinch-zoom the reading viewport on focus.

rules.name: The Hairline-First Rule
rules.body: Resting cards, navigation bars, and list containers establish depth through a `1px` `--line` stroke and a single tonal paper step; apply `shadow-pop` or `shadow-sheet` only to floating popovers, sticky rails, toast notices, and modal sheets that occlude underlying prose.

dos: Do enforce minimum `44×44px` touch targets on `<640px` mobile buttons, tabs, icon switches, and bottom dock controls, honoring `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` under fixed bars.
Do keep dark/tinted custom reader themes isolated inside `[data-reader-surface]` scopes so theme variables invert ink, muted copy, hairlines, and buttons together at WCAG AA contrast.

Do preserve `16px` (`text-base`) input font sizes on mobile viewports, explicit `tabular-nums lining-nums` on chapter numbers and counters, and inline two-step confirmations for destructive bookmark or comment deletions.
Do keep accent color disciplined via warm paper/ink hierarchy and 1px hairline separation before introducing shadows only on floating overlays.
donts: Don't introduce glowing orbs, tilted rotational book cover frames, glassmorphic dark gradients, or decorative dots behind landing headlines.
Don't duplicate navigation controls across both mobile top header and bottom dock simultaneously or allow custom wallpaper images to upload to remote storage.
Don't use `#e4e8f0` (Auto Ink sentinel) directly as a literal dark-text override onto daylight surfaces or hide focus indicators without replacing them cleanly via `:focus-visible`.
Don't mutate cookie keys, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` fallback literals (`"mono"`, `"matte-terminal"`, `"#e4e8f0"`), or CSP/security contracts maintained by `scripts/test-security.ts`.
